channel.title: Twin Lakes Web Co. Blog
channel.description: Practical guidance on websites, local SEO, performance, and small-business technology from Twin Lakes Web Co. in Grayson County, Kentucky.

item.title: Hiring Mistakes That Make Website Projects Harder
item.description: Avoid hiring on appearance or price alone, leaving scope verbal, splitting feedback across staff, and ignoring ownership or maintenance until launch.

item.title: Write a Website Design Brief a Builder Can Quote
item.description: A useful website brief describes the business, audience, customer tasks, pages, required features, content responsibilities, budget, timing, and handoff.

item.title: After Website Launch: Divide Support Responsibilities Clearly
item.description: Assign website support duties after launch, including hosting, updates, backups, and fixes. Define what is covered and how to request help.

item.title: Two School Buses Can’t Pass on This Caneyville Bridge. Kentucky Set Aside $2.79 Million. When Will Work Begin?
item.description: All 12 Caneyville school buses use the narrow U.S. 62 bridge. Kentucky has funded a replacement. Here’s what the road plan says about timing and sidewalks.

item.title: Local or Remote Web Designer: What Should Kentucky Owners Choose?
item.description: Choose a local or remote designer by relevant work, communication, access, and support. Clear delivery terms matter wherever the provider works.

item.title: Managing a Website Project From First Call to Launch
item.description: Manage a website project with a written scope, named decision-maker, content deadlines, review milestones, and customer-task acceptance checks.

item.title: WordPress vs Custom Code: Compare Editing and Maintenance
item.description: A WordPress site can be custom-designed. Compare WordPress and custom code by editing needs, features, maintenance, portability, and support.

item.title: Can You Get a Useful Business Website Under $500?
item.description: A budget under $500 can cover a small website or link page if you limit pages, content work, integrations, and ongoing support.

item.title: Grayson County's Most Profitable Nonprofit Made Nearly $49 Million. Leitchfield Is Still Being Sent Down the Road.
item.description: Nonprofit Owensboro Health Twin Lakes has posted nearly $49 million in surpluses since 2021 while staffing fell and care gaps sent Grayson County patients elsewhere.

item.title: Is Your Website Quote Fair? Evaluate the Scope
item.description: Judge a website quote by comparing the work, deliverables, responsibilities, recurring fees, and risks, not just the price.

item.title: How to Explain Your Website Vision to a Designer
item.description: Translate visual preferences into business goals, customer tasks, content priorities, and a few annotated examples. Explain why each example helps.

item.title: Online Store Template or Custom Development?
item.description: Use a store platform and template when standard workflows fit. Add custom development for requirements those tools cannot meet.

item.title: What SEO Should Be Included in a New Website Build?
item.description: A new website needs crawlable pages, useful content, titles, canonical URLs, a sitemap, internal links, and indexing checks. Ongoing SEO is separate.

item.title: Why Visitors Leave Without Becoming Customers
item.description: Help visitors understand your offer, trust your business, and take the next step. Fix confusion and broken contact paths before buying more traffic.

item.title: Build a Website Faster by Reducing Launch Dependencies
item.description: The safest way to launch faster is to prepare content and accounts early, reduce the first-version scope, and keep functional testing in the plan.

item.title: Web Designer Red Flags You Can Check Before Paying
item.description: Pause when ownership is unclear, scope stays verbal, results are guaranteed without evidence, or the provider cannot explain delivery and support.

item.title: Website Designer vs Developer: Who Does What?
item.description: Designers plan the visual experience; developers build the working site. One person can do both, but every task needs a named owner.

item.title: How to Review a Web Designer’s Portfolio Beyond Appearance
item.description: Open live projects, complete realistic customer tasks, ask what the designer contributed, and compare the work to your required scope.

item.title: What Should a Professional Business Website Include?
item.description: A professional website explains your business and service area, works on phones, supports customer tasks, and has clear ownership and maintenance terms.

item.title: Where to Hire a Web Designer: Comparing Your Options
item.description: Compare referrals, studios, independent designers, agencies, and marketplaces by relevant work, accountability, scope, and ownership.
